newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour's Clark says coalition talks went well.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour's Clark says coalition talks went well.

text.p: Labour leader Helen Clark said on Wednesday the party's first meeting with the New Zealand First negotiating team went well.
"I think we had a good meeting and we are agreed to meet again on Tuesday," Clark told journalists as she left the one and a half hour meeting.
She said Labour would start to work through policy systematically and as fast as possible, but she warned the public to adjust its expectations of how long the process would take.
New Zealand First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election. It is negotiating in parallel with Labour and the ruling conservative National Party over the shape of the new government.
Clark said negotiations would be centred around Tuesdays and Wednesdays. "It will be intensive," she said.

She said each side would prepare its expectations for consultation and how disputes and new issues would be handled when in government because it was important there were no surprises. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473 4746
